title: Hardware
body:

[[Processor]]
#1633-2655 

The physical machine your program eventually runs on: [[Processor]], [[Memory]], storage, and
the I/O devices in between. This course touches it only where C++ makes you notice, which is
three places:

- **Types have sizes** because memory is addressed in [[Byte]]s. See
  [[Address]].
- **Compiled code is machine-specific**, because [[Machine Language]] is per-processor. See
  [[Compiling]].
- **The stack and the heap are two regions of real memory** with different costs. See
  [[Stack and Heap]].

Everything else is deferred. [[COMPUTING MACHINERY]] takes the whole thing apart, and
[[COMPUTING MACHINERY 2]] wires devices onto it; [[OPERATING SYSTEMS]] is the layer that hands
the hardware out to programs so they do not have to ask for it directly.
